solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Jaunty female socialite once performing song

parts.note: a deb, short for debutante, was a young woman launched into society
on stage, performing, is 'on'
an air is a tune or song

explanation.surface: A jaunty society girl of old is singing a number.
explanation.walkthrough: A DEB was a debutante, a young upper-class woman formally presented to society in the old London Season.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone breezily confident and carefree in manner, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Terrible stir about Bill being a prejudiced person

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go round the abbreviation for bill
something terrible is a mess, so the letters of stir are jumbled

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill

explanation.surface: A dreadful row erupts over a bill, and somebody is shown to be a bigot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts the anagram RIST round AC, giving R-AC-IST.
explanation.definitionFit: A bigot who discriminates on grounds of race is a prejudiced person of a specific kind.

clue.text: Advance publicity given to ferocious woman

parts.note: PR stands for public relations, i.e. publicity
an ogress is a female ogre, a fierce woman

explanation.surface: An early bit of press coverage is given to a fearsome lady.
explanation.definitionFit: To make headway or move forward is to advance; the noun senses also match as forward movement.

clue.text: Fruit brought up after one's removed earth

indicators.note: the letter for one is taken away from the result
in a down clue, bringing a word up means writing it from bottom to top

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Some fruit is dug up once a single item is taken away from the soil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought up' turns FRUIT into TIURF; 'removed' takes out I (one), leaving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Turf is grassy topsoil, so it can stand for earth or ground.

clue.text: Shelter unknown character in a deprived area

indicators.note: the unknown letter is placed inside the other pieces, within the poor area

parts.note: a slum is a run-down, poor district
in algebra x, y and z are unknowns, so Y

explanation.surface: Someone nobody knows finds refuge in a poor neighbourhood.
explanation.definitionFit: Asylum is protection or sanctuary granted to someone, the same idea as shelter.

clue.text: Establish arts graduates must have English

parts.note: BA is Bachelor of Arts, plural BAs

explanation.surface: Humanities graduates are told they must have English to set themselves up.
explanation.definitionFit: To base something on a foundation is to establish or ground it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: A stone that's been turned over is huge

indicators.note: turning something over puts it the other way round, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: a gem is a precious stone

explanation.surface: A rock somebody has flipped turns out to be enormous.
explanation.definitionFit: Mega is informal slang for enormous or very great, a synonym of huge.

clue.text: USA sure to get excited about old philosopher

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go round the other piece
excited letters are stirred up, so USA and sure are rearranged

explanation.surface: America is sure to get worked up over a thinker from the past.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of USA SURE gives RUSSEAU; 'about' puts it round O.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean-Jacques Rousseau was an eighteenth-century Genevan thinker, author of The Social Contract.

clue.text: Intimidating company faction

parts.note: a wing of a party is a faction within it

explanation.surface: A business group within a firm is behaving like a bully.
explanation.definitionFit: Cowing someone means frightening them into submission, which is to intimidate.

clue.text: Facing change, see female wobble

indicators.note: the letter for female sits in front of, facing, the word for change

parts.note: to alter is to change

explanation.surface: Confronted with change, a woman is seen to waver.
explanation.definitionFit: To falter is to waver or lose steadiness, the same as wobbling.

clue.text: Quiet deed brings agreement

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quietly
an act is a deed

explanation.surface: A discreet good turn leads to two sides seeing eye to eye.
explanation.definitionFit: A pact is a formal treaty or accord between parties, so a kind of agreement.

clue.text: Reckon car may go across motorway after spinning round

indicators.note: the word for the car spans the other piece, which sits inside it

parts.note: an estate is an estate car, a station wagon

indicators.note: spinning round turns the motorway's letters back to front

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's first major motorway, written here as MI

explanation.surface: A driver works out whether the car can cross the motorway after a spin.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is Britain's first long motorway, written with the 1 read as a letter I; 'after spinning round' turns it back to front, and 'may go across' sets it inside the car.
explanation.definitionFit: To estimate is to calculate roughly or judge, a sense of reckon.

clue.text: Chucking object containing string

indicators.note: the word for object holds the other piece within it

parts.note: a thing is an object
a row is a line or string of things

explanation.surface: An item is tossed away with some twine inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Throwing and chucking both mean tossing something through the air.

clue.text: Aroused? This may suggest no!

parts.note: the two letters of 'no', turned round, read as the word on

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a person is excited, then flatly says no.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as an instruction: the word 'on' turned back to front gives 'no'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an informal idiom for being stimulated or excited, especially sexually.

clue.text: Supporting insincere person, one puts forward an idea

parts.note: pro means in favour of
a poser is someone putting on an act

explanation.surface: Backing a phoney, someone floats a suggestion.
explanation.definitionFit: A proposer moves a motion or suggestion, so someone tabling a plan.

clue.text: What to expect — badly penned column

indicators.note: the other piece is shut inside, like an animal in a pen

parts.note: par is the normal or expected standard
ill means badly, as in ill-treated

explanation.surface: Someone warns what to expect: a newspaper column written poorly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'column' is architectural here, not a newspaper piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A pillar is an upright support post in a building, which is a column.

clue.text: Opponent of Henry VIII to a greater extent

definitions.meaning: Sir Thomas ..., Lord Chancellor, was executed for refusing to accept the king as head of the Church
an adverb meaning further or in larger measure

explanation.definitionFit: Thomas More opposed the king's break with Rome; separately, the word is the comparative of much.

clue.text: Crush has fellow getting broken leg

parts.note: a man is a fellow

indicators.note: broken letters are rearranged, so leg is jumbled

explanation.surface: An infatuated man ends up with a broken leg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crush' looks like a romantic infatuation but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To mangle something is to squash or mutilate it badly, a sense of crush.

clue.text: Talk about the French holiday home?

indicators.note: the word for talk goes around the French article

parts.note: a chat is a talk
le is French for the

explanation.surface: People chat about the French place they stay on vacation.
explanation.definitionFit: A chalet is a wooden mountain cabin, often rented to holidaymakers.

clue.text: House with old books — indication of wise old bird?

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for house
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: A building full of antique books has a wise owl inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An owl's call is its signature cry, and the owl is the proverbial wise old bird.

clue.text: Work until 1.50

parts.note: to can mean until, as in nine to five
in Roman numerals 1 is I and 50 is L

explanation.surface: Someone is stuck at work until ten to two.
explanation.walkthrough: 1.50 looks like a time, but it is read as two Roman numerals.
explanation.definitionFit: Toil is hard labour, so it is a synonym of work.

clue.text: Pale-looking old rocker sought by police?

parts.note: wan means pale and sickly
a Ted or Teddy boy was a 1950s rock-and-roll youth in Britain

explanation.surface: A pasty ageing rock fan is on the run from the law.
explanation.walkthrough: Teddy boys were a 1950s British youth cult with drape jackets and rock and roll.
explanation.definitionFit: A suspect on a police wanted list is being sought by officers.

clue.text: Member of club managed to contain a riot somehow

indicators.note: the word for managed holds the jumbled letters inside

parts.note: ran a business means managed it

indicators.note: somehow suggests a muddled order, so a riot is rearranged

explanation.surface: A club member managed to keep a disturbance under control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges the letters of 'a riot', and 'to contain' puts that jumble inside the word for managed, split after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotary International is a service club; each of its members has this title.

clue.text: Stupid person gets the bird

definitions.meaning: the diver, a large waterbird, is known by this name in North America

explanation.surface: A fool is mocked and jeered.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is slang for a crazy person and also the name of a diving water bird.
